The disappearance of ChIP peaks when switching from PFA alone to PFA+DSG fixation suggests that these peaks are artifacts of the single crosslinking method. Formaldehyde (PFA) crosslinks proteins to DNA but can also generate non-specific background, particularly in open chromatin regions such as active promoters and enhancers, where abundant transcription factors and RNA polymerases are prone to crosslinking. The addition of DSG, a protein-protein crosslinker, stabilizes chromatin structure and reduces such non-specific background, thereby eliminating artifact peaks. True binding sites of IKAROS are expected to be captured by both methods, so the disappearing peaks are most likely located at active regulatory elements.
